clue.text: One who shuts up having caught out failure

indicators.note: out says the letter for caught is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: someone who shuts things up, e.g. a shop at night, is a closer
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A shop-closer who has been caught out is labelled a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who fails, who never wins, is commonly called a loser.

clue.text: Trap undermining flashy gossip

indicators.note: undermining places the trap word under the flashy word in this down entry

parts.note: loud means flashy, as of garish clothes
trap is slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'

explanation.surface: A snare is set to discredit a showy rumour-monger.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip who talks indiscreetly and noisily is a loudmouth.

clue.text: Leader in Strictly now appearing in extremely prestigious balls

indicators.note: leader in picks the first letter of Strictly
appearing in puts the now word between those outer letters
extremely picks the outermost letters of prestigious

parts.note: here means now, as in 'here and now'

explanation.surface: A Strictly Come Dancing star turns up at grand society balls.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Come Dancing is a BBC ballroom dancing show.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls are round objects, and spheres are perfectly round solids.

clue.text: Man from Armagh regularly holding record

indicators.note: holding says the regular letters wrap round the record
regularly picks alternate letters of Armagh, starting with the first

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A man from Northern Ireland's Armagh keeps hold of an old record.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph is a male first name, so a fellow or man.

clue.text: Second team getting food before minor fixture

indicators.note: before places the food word ahead of the team words

parts.note: grub is slang for food
a crew is a team, as of rowers

explanation.surface: A reserve side eats before a lesser match on the sporting calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixture' suggests a sports match, as does 'Second team'; here it is a small screw that fastens things.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub screw is a small headless screw, a minor piece of hardware that fixes parts together.

clue.text: Run over side, almost, clutching extremely big sail

indicators.note: over places the run word on top in this down entry

parts.note: to run is to go

indicators.note: clutching says the shortened side holds the outsize letters
almost says the side word loses its last letter

parts.note: a side is a team
OS stands for outsize, clothing for the extremely big

explanation.surface: A sailor runs over the side clutching a huge sail.
explanation.walkthrough: TEA (TEAM less M) holds OS, the clothing size abbreviation for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: To sail on a voyage, or join the navy, is to go to sea.

clue.text: Announcement of instrument to rule European republic

indicators.note: announcement says the words are spoken, so it is their sound that counts

parts.note: a uke is a ukulele, an instrument, and to reign is to rule

explanation.surface: A ruler is proclaimed in a European republic, with music.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is a republic in Eastern Europe.

clue.text: Remove question for head of maths in term

indicators.note: for says the question letters replace the letter of maths

parts.note: a semester is a university term

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of maths

explanation.surface: A school drops a question from the maths syllabus in the middle of term.
explanation.definitionFit: To sequester is to set aside or take away, to remove something from use.

clue.text: Concerned with a foreign airline that's brought up alcohol

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: brought up, in this down entry, reads the airline word upwards

parts.note: El Al is Israel's national airline

explanation.surface: A worry about an overseas airline that allows drink on board.
explanation.walkthrough: REAL ALE is traditional cask-conditioned British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is beer, which is an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Handle an old wit, the last to be promoted

indicators.note: promoted says the final letter moves up the down entry

parts.note: Oscar Wilde was a famous Victorian wit

explanation.surface: A manager deals with a witty veteran, the last in line for promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: WILDE's final E moves up to give WIELD.
explanation.definitionFit: To wield a tool or weapon is to handle it, to use it with skill.

clue.text: Finished potential holder for piece in pad

parts.note: up means finished, as in 'time is up'
piece is slang for a gun, and a holster holds a gun

explanation.surface: A cushion is sought to hold a chess piece or ornament snugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' is gangster slang for a handgun.
explanation.definitionFit: To pad furniture with stuffing and cover it is to upholster it.

clue.text: Major disturbance caused by EU stepping out of line about a king

indicators.note: about says what is left of the line goes around a and the king letter
stepping out of says the two letters EU leave the line word

parts.note: a queue is a line of waiting people
the European Union's letters, taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Brexit as an upheaval: the EU leaves the queue, with royalty involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Brexit; 'stepping out of' leaves QUE, and 'about' wraps it round A and K.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthquake, or by extension any great upheaval, is a quake.

clue.text: Securing non-European terminal, army invades abandoned island

indicators.note: securing means holding, so the rearranged letters hold the shortened terminal word
abandoned, meaning wild and unrestrained, signals the letters of army invades rearranged
non-European says the letter E for European is dropped

parts.note: an earth is an electrical terminal connected to the ground

explanation.surface: Soldiers seize a terminus and then storm a deserted island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminal' suggests a station or airport, but it is an electrical earth; 'non-European' leaves ARTH, which 'Securing' holds within the 'abandoned' letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha's Vineyard is an island off Cape Cod in Massachusetts.

clue.text: Puts up rafter, not all of it as above

indicators.note: not all of it says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A builder fixes a roof beam, but only part of it, as stated earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Ut supra is Latin for 'as above', used in documents to refer back to earlier text.

clue.text: Narrow glass container, mostly pink around interior

indicators.note: interior says the turned pink goes inside the container word

parts.note: a phial is a small glass bottle

indicators.note: around turns the shortened pink word backwards
mostly says the pink word loses its last letter

parts.note: coral is a shade of pink

explanation.surface: A slim bottle, its inside tinged pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' and 'around' turn the pink shade into AROC, which 'interior' sets inside the bottle; 'Narrow' is an adjective here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A parochial view is narrow, limited to a small local outlook.

clue.text: Strict unopened communication about the setter

indicators.note: unopened says the first letter of the communication word is removed

parts.note: a text is a message sent by phone
re means about, concerning
the setter refers to themself, so me

explanation.surface: A setter complains about a severe message left unread.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe or uncompromising measures can be called strict or extreme.

clue.text: Basic lease isn't up for renewal

indicators.note: a renewal remakes something, so the letters of lease isn't are remade in a new order

explanation.surface: A tenant notes that a simple lease has not yet come up for renewal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential is fundamental, the basic core of a thing.

clue.text: Yorkshire village wife's put in a very little amount when pressure's off

indicators.note: put in says the wife letter goes inside
off says the pressure letter is taken away

parts.note: a ha'porth (halfpennyworth) is a tiny amount
P is the physics symbol for pressure
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife contributes a pittance to a village fund once the strain eases.
explanation.walkthrough: A HA'PORTH is a halfpenny's worth, British for a trifling amount. Haworth is the Brontës' home village.
explanation.definitionFit: Haworth is a village in West Yorkshire, famous as home of the Brontë sisters.

clue.text: Attorney stopping payment as a measure of power?

indicators.note: stopping, as a plug stops a hole, puts the attorney inside the payment

parts.note: a wage is a payment for work
ATT is a short form of attorney

explanation.surface: A lawyer blocks a pay packet as a show of power.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that power here is electrical, not influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattage is electrical power expressed in watts.

clue.text: I for one ring back, say, before noon

indicators.note: before places the earlier pieces ahead of the noon letter

parts.note: a halo is a ring of light

indicators.note: back says the say letters are turned around

parts.note: eg (for example) means say

explanation.surface: Someone promises to ring back before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the chemical symbol for iodine, a halogen; 'I for one' looks like the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodine is an example of a halogen, one of the reactive non-metal elements.

clue.text: Brief role: a small boy is showing off

indicators.note: brief says the role word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a part is an actor's role
Des is a short form of the boy's name Desmond

explanation.surface: A child given a tiny part in a play shows off.
explanation.definitionFit: To parade something is to display it ostentatiously, to show it off.

clue.text: Supporters wrongfully blocking standard entrance to stadium

indicators.note: blocking puts the wrongfully word inside the standard word

parts.note: par is a standard, as in 'up to par'
ill means wrongly, as in 'ill-gotten'

indicators.note: entrance to picks the first letter of stadium

explanation.surface: Fans wrongly obstruct the entry to a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' hints at football fans; they are columns.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillars are columns that support the weight of a structure.

clue.text: Old engineer's design left during communist revolt

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the name to the rest

indicators.note: during puts the design and left letters inside
revolt here means turned over, so the communist word is reversed

parts.note: red is a communist
an aim is a design or intention

explanation.surface: A historic engineer's plan devised during a communist uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Gottlieb Daimler was a nineteenth-century German motor engineer and car pioneer.

clue.text: Cause of misapprehension of coalition — one pulls out

indicators.note: out, as in 'out of order', signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A coalition partner withdraws, revealing a misunderstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A trick of the eye makes us perceive something falsely, a misapprehension.

clue.text: No time for toast — it's water you may find here

indicators.note: no time for says every letter for time is removed from toast

parts.note: it's expands to 'it is', supplying is

explanation.surface: No time for breakfast toast; you may find water here instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Ts leave TOAST, giving OAS.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert where a spring or well provides drinking supply.

clue.text: Drug found in meal, but not initially

indicators.note: not initially says the meal word loses its first letter

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A drug is slipped into food, though not at first.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper is slang for a stimulant such as amphetamine.

clue.text: African fascist changing direction

indicators.note: changing direction says one compass point is swapped for another: north for south-west

parts.note: a Nazi is a fascist

explanation.surface: A fascist turns around and goes another way.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swazi is a native of Eswatini (Swaziland) in southern Africa.

clue.text: Girl rudely interrupted by Dutch artist and jazz musician

indicators.note: interrupted by says the artist goes into the middle of the shuffled girl
rudely, meaning roughly, signals the letters of girl are shuffled

parts.note: Karel Appel was a Dutch painter

explanation.surface: A girl is rudely cut off mid-sentence by a painter and a jazzman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rudely' looks like manners but signals the shuffle, giving GRIL; 'interrupted by' splits it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stéphane Grappelli was a celebrated French jazz violinist.

clue.text: Dogs also found in Jewish villages, not the first time

indicators.note: found in says the also word sits inside
not the first says the earlier of the two time letters is dropped

parts.note: shtetls were small Jewish towns in Eastern Europe
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Dogs were also kept in old Jewish villages, though not at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' removes only the earlier of the two Ts, giving SHETLS; 'found in' places the also word before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Shetland sheepdogs, called shelties or Shetlands, are a breed of dog.

clue.text: Pastoral feature of Russia, in short

parts.note: R is a short form of Russia
the Ural mountains and river are a feature of the Russian landscape

explanation.surface: A countryside landmark of Russia, described briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Urals are the mountain range dividing European and Asian Russia, so 'feature of Russia' leans on Russia twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral life is country life, the rural sort with farms and flocks.
